user.title: Choose the board
user.description: These are the Tasmota boards announcing themselves on your broker. Choose the one with the infrared emitters.

manual.title: Enter the topic
manual.description: Use the Topic value from the board's MQTT settings. Leave FullTopic alone unless you changed it on the board.

abort.already_configured: This board is already set up.
abort.mqtt_unavailable: MQTT is not available. Set up the MQTT integration first.

user.title: Add appliance
user.description: A television, a sound bar, a fan: anything whose keys you learn one by one. It appears under the board with its own device, and every key you learn becomes a button on it.

data_description.name: The name you will see on the device and use as device in the remote actions.
data_description.channel: The emitter pointed at this appliance, counted in the order of the board template. It can be changed later without learning anything again.

added.title: {name} is ready
added.description: Learn its first key now, or finish and learn later from Manage appliance.

reconfigure.title: {name}
reconfigure.description: What do you want to do with {name}?

learn.title: Learn a command
learn.description: What is the key called? Give it a short name, such as power or volume up. After you continue, point the remote at the board and press that key once. Holding it is fine; two different keys in a row are not.

data_description.command: Becomes the name of the button, on the {name} device.

learned.title: {command} learned
learned.description: The button is there, on the {name} device. Learn the next key, or finish.

learn_timeout.title: Nothing arrived
learn_timeout.description: The board heard no usable key in 30 seconds. Check that the remote points at the receiver and press the key once, on its own: a key pressed from too far away arrives broken and is thrown away.

learn_hvac.title: That is an air conditioner remote
learn_hvac.description: One capture from an air conditioner remote is one temperature in one mode, so a button made from it would always send the same thing. Add the unit with Add air conditioner instead, which reads the vendor from this same remote and builds every command.

learn_too_large.title: The code is too large
learn_too_large.description: This key arrived as a raw code larger than the board can send in one MQTT message, so a button made from it would never work.

delete_command.title: Delete a learned command
delete_command.description: The button of the command goes with it, and it can be learned again from scratch.

channel.title: Change the emitter
channel.description: Every command of {name} leaves through the new emitter from now on. Nothing has to be learned again.

rename.title: Rename
rename.description: The buttons, the codes and the emitter stay as they are.

progress.wait_for_key:
Point the remote of {name} at the board and press {command} once.

Waiting up to 30 seconds.

error.name_taken: Another appliance of this board already has this name.

abort.board_not_loaded: The board is not running right now. Check that it is online, then try again.
abort.no_receiver: This board has no IRrecv GPIO assigned, so it cannot learn. Assign one in the Tasmota template and reload the integration.
abort.no_commands: Nothing has been learned for this appliance yet.
abort.command_deleted: {command} was deleted, together with its button.

user.title: Add air conditioner
user.description: Nothing is learned key by key here. The firmware knows the protocol of dozens of vendors and builds every command from mode, temperature, fan and vane. In the next step you press any key of the unit's own remote, and the firmware reads the vendor and the model from it, so there is nothing to look up in a manual.

data_description.channel: The emitter pointed at this appliance, counted in the order of the board template. It can be changed later without learning anything again.

read_failed.title: No air conditioner frame
read_failed.description: Press one key of the remote of {name}, pointed at the receiver, one key at a time. Anything that is not an air conditioner frame is ignored while the window is open, broken frames included, so nothing else can end the wait. A remote that is not an air conditioner does not work here: add those with Add appliance.

reconfigure.title: {name}
reconfigure.description: {vendor}, model {model}. What do you want to do?

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: What the firmware is told about {name}, a {vendor} unit.

data_description.model: Some vendors make several remotes that look alike to the decoder, and the model decides what the firmware sends. If the vane does not respond, try another model here. For LG, AKB74955603 is the one that sends the vane; Read the remote again, pressing the vane key, sets it by itself.
data_description.hvac_modes: Only the modes your unit really has. Off is always there.
data_description.swing_vertical: Offer the vane positions on the card. Off by default for vendors where the vane is a toggle, because there every command would flip it.
data_description.swing_horizontal: Only for units with a horizontal vane that the remote controls.

channel.title: Change the emitter
channel.description: Every command of {name} leaves through the new emitter from now on. Nothing has to be learned again.

rename.title: Rename
rename.description: The buttons, the codes and the emitter stay as they are.

progress.wait_for_key:
Point the remote of {name} at the board and press any key.

Waiting up to 30 seconds.

error.name_taken: Another appliance of this board already has this name.
error.no_hvac_frame: No air conditioner frame was decoded.
error.temp_range: The highest temperature has to be above the lowest.
error.no_modes: Choose at least one mode besides off.

abort.board_not_loaded: The board is not running right now. Check that it is online, then try again.
abort.no_receiver: This board has no IRrecv GPIO assigned, so it cannot learn. Assign one in the Tasmota template and reload the integration.
